Serial lookup: Squier and Fender

Type a serial number and press Go. The tool reads the prefix, estimates the year and factory, then lists the most likely series with its typical specs and prices. Works offline.

Try:

Where to find the serial: on the neck plate on the back of the body, on the back of the headstock (many Squier and Mexican Fender), or on the front headstock decal (Japan JV/SQ). Pre-1965 Fender numbers are on the neck plate.

How the search works: the serial is cleaned, split into parts and matched against the rule list; unknown prefixes get a labelled guess from their letters; look-alike glyphs (O/0/C, I/1, S/5), a dropped extra character or a swapped pair are tried automatically, each repair gets an accuracy index, and a clearly better reading replaces the typed one (with a button to undo it); suggestions are ranked by year fit, model popularity and any filters you set, and shown as a share of the total likelihood.

How reliable is this? A serial gives you the factory and the year. It cannot tell you the model, so the series shown is the most likely one for that factory and year. Specs and prices are typical values (confidence is shown for each reading). Confirm with the neck-heel date, pot codes and the headstock decal. Prices are estimates in USD; check Reverb and eBay sold listings for real values.

Extending it: everything is in two arrays near the bottom of this file, RULES (serial patterns) and MODELS (specs). Add rows to grow the database. Photos live in PHOTOS (one reference photo per body type, re-tinted per finish). Database v0.4.
